verdicts.reason: Structural description of the top module; nothing to verify or exercise in simulation.

Quote states round-robin AR/AW arbitration as responsibility; the rule is stated and a scenario applies. The fields are acceptable, but the quote is a description, so keep it only with the simultaneous-request condition. Fields are right.
Backpressure stalling the owning sequencer is DUT behavior, not a master obligation. The actor should be system. The master merely applies backpressure.
Quote states the owner is retained through the final R/B. It is checkable by scenario and by assertion on grant stability.
Quote directly states the read flow, one APB read per beat in order, and holding the response until RREADY.
Quote states accepting AW then W beats in order.
Quote says WVALID may precede AW. This is a permitted stimulus that a scenario should exercise.
Quote states WREADY remains low until AW is accepted. It is checkable every cycle from interface signals.
Quote states one APB write per beat and B returned after the last APB completion.
Quote states one owner at a time and no read/write interleaving.
APB transfers are sequential is bridge behavior as APB master, so actor should be system. The master actor is wrong because the bridge itself is the APB master.
The bridge drives APB payload and control. The actor is the bridge (system), not the AXI master.
Quote states IDs are retained and echoed unchanged. The RID/BID mapping is a reasonable reading.
Quote states the read count is ARLEN+1 and the legal write count is AWLEN+1.
Quote states AXI response payload stability while VALID=1 and READY=0. It is checkable every cycle.

duplicates.reason: Both come from the same quote about sequential APB transfers and stable payload; the sequential rule is only loosely distinct. Do not merge if sequentiality is verified separately.
Both concern single transaction ownership. AB-5.4-01 adds read/write non-interleaving, so merge is questionable.

questions.question: Does 'APB transfers are sequential' mean one APB access fully completes before the next starts, with no pipelining? Is a gap needed between transfers?
What is the round-robin policy when only one of AR/AW is pending, and how is the arbitration turn updated after a grant?
What response does the bridge return for an illegal write count (the quote says 'legal write count is AWLEN+1')? How are illegal lengths handled?
